input.question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?
input.ground_truth: F-35 is pretty much 3 different planes, that look similar. * Navy version has different wings and modifications to frame to support carrier landing. * Marine version has VSTOL. * Air Force version has better performance.

Question: How come the F-35 program cost way more to develop than the F-22 despite being generally less technologically advanced?

response.prediction:
Okay, let's imagine you want to build a really cool toy car, and your friend wants to build a different cool toy car.

Let’s say your toy car (the F-22) is super special and has lots of new, fancy parts that no one has ever made before. You have to invent those parts, which takes a lot of time and money. But once you figure out how to make them, you can make more of those cars a little bit easier, because you already know how to do it.

Now, your friend’s toy car (the F-35) is also really cool, but your friend wants this toy car to be able to play with kids in different countries, so your friend has to make the toy car fit lots and lots of different rules from all those countries. That means your friend has to change the toy car again and again, and sometimes even start over a little bit to make it work for everyone. Also, lots of other kids want to play with this toy car, so your friend has to make LOTS and LOTS of them, not just a few.

Even though your friend’s toy car isn’t as fancy as yours in some ways, all the changing and making for many different people costs a LOT more money and takes much longer. That’s why your friend’s toy car costs way more to make, even if it isn’t as “advanced” in some ways.
